_doc: Skirmish economy (plan: Sectors and settlements, Key skirmish mechanics). Times in seconds, distances in world pixels. capture_speed: settlements are taken this many times faster than their capture_time. militia_guard_radius: neutral militia go for any enemy this close (and anyone who hurts them), chase at most 1.5x as far from their post, then walk back.

pile_amounts._doc: How much each resource pile holds before it runs dry (rare = every faction rare and gems). Piles in a home sector hold home_factor times as much, so the start is not a race against the clock. -1 makes piles endless.

hall_defense._doc: The hall shoots 'arrows' (per hall level) at enemies within range px; height is the roof in metres, for the view. A capital cannot be captured: it has 'hp' hit points (one value per hall level, I-IV) behind armor_pct armour, a body of 'radius' px, and mends mend_per_second once mend_after seconds pass without a hit. When it falls its owner has lost.

building_defense._doc: Unit buildings (dwellings and faction buildings) can be torn down. A dwelling has hp_base + hp_per_tier x (its lowest tier - 1) hit points, x upgraded_factor once any of its upgrades is bought; a faction building has special_hp. A site under construction starts at start_share of them and grows with the work. armor_pct, mend_after and mend_per_second as for the hall. When one falls its queue is lost and its ground opens again.

dwelling_slots_doc: Which tiers share one dwelling (one queue, the art of its first tier; each tier keeps its own upgrade). The art of the other tiers (dwellings[1], dwellings[3]) is free for the faction buildings.

faction_buildings._doc: Two buildings per faction in the art the shared dwellings freed (dwellings[1] and dwellings[3]). hall: hall level needed; limit: how many a player may own. effect.kind: aura (own: heal per second as a share of max health, statuses on own units; foe: statuses on enemies; sight: px it sees beyond its footprint), tower (arrows like a hall), raise (enemies dying within radius rise as unit for seconds, at most max at once), trade (a button: pay 'give' for 'take'; worker: true spends a worker), market (a button per pair: pay amount of one for rate x amount of another), gate (a button: units within radius of the partner, the hall or another gate of the same id, step out here; cooldown), research (a button, once: every unit of yours takes taken_factor of the damage), feast (a button: every soldier of yours gets the status for seconds; cooldown), income (resource per minute), spawn (every seconds a unit with no worker, at most max alive from it). Statuses as SimUnit.status kinds; radius in px.

worker_upgrades._doc: Bought at a finished storehouse, one track per resource the faction gathers (gold comes from settlements and has none). Each level adds bonus[level-1] to the loads workers deliver of that resource (+15%, +30%, +50% in all), for good and for every worker. Level n costs cost[n-1] and takes seconds[n-1] at that storehouse, which works on one upgrade at a time; it needs hall level hall[n-1]. A track for a rare resource also costs rare[n-1] of that resource.

dwelling_upgrade._doc: A dwelling's permanent upgrade: from then on it trains its tier's upgraded unit (units.json 'upgrade'). Costs base + per_tier x tier of each resource; from tier rare_from_tier on, also rare_per_tier x (tier - rare_from_tier + 1) of the faction's own rare. The dwelling trains nothing while it is being upgraded.

twists._doc: Faction twists (plan: Key skirmish mechanics). no_worker_tiers: these tiers train without drafting a worker, while fewer than raised_base + raised_per_sector x sectors of them are alive (then they need a worker like any unit); raised_time_factor / raised_gold_factor make those worker-free units slower and dearer. capture_time_factor: enemies need this much longer to take your settlements. plunder: gold this faction takes when it captures a settlement, by settlement size. unit_gold_factor: this faction's troops cost that much more gold. regen_near (forest or water) / regen_reach (px) / regen_per_second: units this close to woods or water heal that share of their health per second. road_speed_factor: this faction marches that much faster on roads. gather_factor: {resource: factor} for loads this faction's workers deliver. sight_factor: this faction's units spot enemies that much farther away. first_strike_factor: a blow on an enemy still at full health deals that much more. kill_heal: a unit that lands a killing blow heals that share of its health.

capture_decay._doc: A half-taken settlement nobody is taking recovers at this many times its capture speed: empty = no one there, defended = its owner's troops (or neutral militia) are back.

ai_difficulty._doc: Computer players: think_every = seconds between decisions; first_wave = army size before the first attack; wave_growth = added to it after each wave. expand = capture squads it sends out at once to take free settlements (0 = they wait for the waves). attack_edge = strength ratio (EconomyAi.power_of) a wave needs over its target's defenders, also over the rival armies before it storms a capital (0 = it counts heads). regroup_ratio = a wave whose strength falls below this share of the foes around it runs back to the capital (0 = never). protect_rank = veterans of this rank or more retreat home when below retreat_hp of their health and rest until rejoin_hp (0 = never). hall_army = soldiers it keeps before raising the hall (+2 per hall level). income_bonus = extra share of every load and of settlement gold (the one level that cheats).

forts._doc: Walls (Fortifications). A wall order is a line of cells cut into pieces of piece_cells; each piece costs 'wall' cost and is built by workers. A finished piece can become a gate (opens for its owner's units) or a tower (holds up to 'garrison' ranged units that shoot farther and only ranged and flying foes can hurt). Ends snap onto rock, water or walls within snap_cells. No wall cell within settlement_clearance px of a settlement centre, or within enemy_clearance px of an enemy's.
